piece: Denormal flush and special results in `v_rcp_f32`, `v_rsq_f32`, `v_sqrt_f32`, `v_log_f32`, `v_exp_f32`, `v_rcp_iflag_f32`
sentences: Measured on an RX 6800 (gfx1030, not the console's gfx1013) with raw kernels in both wave sizes and all four IEEE/DX10_CLAMP combinations: all six read a denormal input as a zero of its sign and flush a denormal result, even with MODE's denormal field set to keep them.

`v_rcp_f32(±0)` = ±inf, `v_rsq_f32(-0)` = -inf, `v_sqrt_f32(-0)` = -0, `v_log_f32(±0)` = -inf, `v_rcp_f32(FLT_MAX)` = +0, `v_exp_f32(-127)` = +0, `v_exp_f32(128)` = +inf, and every invalid result (`v_sqrt_f32`/`v_rsq_f32`/`v_log_f32` of a negative, …) is `0xffc00000`.
Each is within 1 ulp of correctly rounded on the values tried, and `v_rcp_iflag_f32` is bit-identical to `v_rcp_f32`.

**Not modelled yet:** the translator leaves all six on Vulkan's default denormal handling, and the ±0 and negative inputs above stay undefined in the emitted SPIR-V (`OpFDiv` by zero, `Sqrt`/`Log2` of a negative), as listed in the multiply-add and output modifiers row; the `clamp`/`omod` bits on `v_cvt_f32_*` and `v_rcp_iflag_f32` are modelled there.
Source: [@shelbykb2's hardware words](https://github.com/ItsNotRexed/Leonida/issues/634#issuecomment-7074348963), not the ISA text.

The corpus only ever writes MODE's FP_ROUND field and carries `mul:2`/`mul:4`/`div:2` on 102,365 float instructions (a compiler does not emit one that is ignored), so the inferred f32 state, IEEE off with denormals flushed, is the one to model.

Corpus count (`tools/shader_profile.py`, 26,503 shaders; the shader count of each op deduplicates its `_e32`/`_e64` forms): `v_rcp_f32` 17,393 shaders / 424,863 occurrences, `v_rsq_f32` 17,221 / 269,310, `v_sqrt_f32` 14,511 / 201,422, `v_log_f32` 8,454 / 90,199, `v_exp_f32` 8,603 / 148,846, `v_rcp_iflag_f32` 7,395 / 34,852; 20,193 shaders (76.2%) use at least one, 1,169,492 occurrences (2.6% of the corpus's 44,406,870 instructions).
